text.p: Madagascar's former military ruler Didier Ratsiraka was declared winner of the country's presidential election by the High Constitutional Court on Friday.
Ending weeks of suspense, the court announced that Ratsiraka won 50.7 percent of the vote in last December's election compared with 49.3 for Albert Zafy.
Retired Admiral Ratsiraka, 60, ruled the world's fourth-largest island from 1975 to 1992 when he was defeated by Zafy in Madagascar's first multi-party polls.

The army warned on Thursday it would not tolerate violence by supporters of the beaten candidate. It moved armoured cars onto the streets of the capital Antananarivo late on Thursday to back up the warning.
The early elections were ordered after 69-year-old Zafy was impeached by parliament last year for repeated violations of the constitution.
He and Ratsiraka came top of a first round of voting last November 3 and then went into a head-to-head contest on December 29.
